construction: 53 parts in 14 steps plus six children. Steps 7 and 9: two 5×5 corner-round curved-top bricks facing −Z and +Z make the bark. Children `Step 79` (step 10) and `Steps 83 to 89` (step 14): 1×1 bricks with studs on four sides, plus animal tails as the bent roots and branches. Step 13: a frog, leaves and flowers.
interfaces: The parent matrix `0 1 0 / −1 0 0 / 0 0 1` turns it 90° about Z. Measured: in its own frame the trunk lies along X, 262 LDU long and 172 high; in the parent that length becomes its height (y −318 to −56). Stud directions: 53 parts in all six directions: 10 up, 6 down, 9 +X, 11 −X, 6 +Z, 5 −Z, 6 angled. It has the corpus's top SNOT score.
lesson: An organic shape built in a convenient frame, with animal tails as roots.
parent_context: The tree trunk beside the well in `21325 - Medieval Blacksmith.ldr`. The leaf canopy above it belongs to another section.
reuse_notes: Build tall organic shapes lying down where the studs help, then stand them up. Look for unusual parts, such as animal tails, for roots and branches.
